human_name: HLA-C class-I locus (polymorphic, KIR ligand, gene-conversion-prone)

GRCh38.note: HLA-C gene body on PGF reference haplotype; ~85 kb upstream of HLA-B

architecture_note: HLA-C is the third classical class-I gene, slightly less polymorphic than HLA-A/B but still hyperdiverse. Same complex_mosaic rationale as HLA-A/B.

exon_2.note: Hyperpolymorphic. See IPD-IMGT/HLA for PSVs (CC-BY-ND, no inline copy).

exon_3.note: Hyperpolymorphic. Includes the C1/C2 dimorphism (Asn80/Lys80) that determines KIR2DL1/2/3 ligand specificity.

diagnostic_features.snp_density_note: HLA-C has >6700 distinct alleles (IPD-IMGT/HLA Release 3.55+, 2024). Coding-region nt identity to HLA-B is ~88 %, leading to cross-locus mapping ambiguity.

ipd_imgt_reference.use: Resolve allele-specific PSVs via API at runtime

gene_conversion_evidence.note: HLA-C↔HLA-B inter-locus gene conversion is documented (Parham 1989; Chen 2007). The C1/C2 KIR-ligand dimorphism likely arose by gene conversion from HLA-B.

diagnostic_features.clinical_associations_note: HLA-C*06:02 (psoriasis); HLA-C alleles determine KIR-ligand specificity → NK cell function, transplantation, HIV control.

primary.note: Mirrors HLA-A/B. HLA-C reads cross-map heavily to HLA-B (~88 % nt identity).

primary_sources.note: Norman PJ et al., Genome Res — 95 MHC haplotypes
Horton R et al., Immunogenetics — MHC Haplotype Project
Robinson J et al., maintainers; CC-BY-ND, external reference only
